text: This diagram illustrates the complete process of note-making. To make bank notes, the first step is to properly design it. While background color and art work are thoroughly considered, security issues are one thing that we cannot over look either. After this, metal plates need to be prepared by skilled machinists so as to proceed to bank notes printing, in which stage sheets are used to print (each containing 50 bank notes). Also, special ink is printed on both side of the sheet and the images are slightly raised. Then comes the most important stage -- inspection.

In this step, workers are needed to manually inspect the quality of sheets and divide them into three groups: good quality, partially damaged quality and bad quality. Sheets in the second groups then get seperated into good ones, which, together with good quality sheets, enter a process of packaging and distribution where seperate notes are cut and finally enter the market, and bad ones, which go to disposal with bad quality sheets, where both groups get securely destroyed. This leads us to a conclusion that the process of bank notes creation is secure as well as simple.

The Last Thing I Remembered It happened on a Tuesday, which seemed unfair. Gods deserve better days than Tuesdays. I was standing in the checkout line at a grocery store in Fresno, holding a carton of eggs and a coupon for laundry detergent, when the knowledge arrived. It did not feel like a thought. It felt like remembering my own phone number. Oh, right. I am God. The stars, the platypus, the particular shade of orange on the fruit stand across the aisle, all of it came from me. I had simply stepped away for a while.

The woman in front of me was arguing with the cashier about a banana. Not the price, just the banana, which she said had been sold to her as organic. I felt a wave of tenderness for her so large that my knees went weak. I knew the exact number of her hairs. I knew she had cried in her car that morning and not told anyone why. The eggs slipped out of my hand. Twelve of them broke on the linoleum. "Sir?" said the cashier. "Are you okay?" "I made you," I said.

Eastern Europe, here comes the cavalry. The U.S. Army says it will soon be sending armored Stryker vehicles on a 1,100-mile convoy through six European countries to show solidarity to allies in the wake of recent Russian actions in the Ukraine and Crimea that have Eastern Europe on edge. The move was first reported Thursday in the military newspaper Stars and Stripes. U.S. Army Europe posted the Stripes story on its website on Friday.

The convoy is "a highly visible demonstration of U.S, commitment to its NATO allies and demonstrating NATO's ability to move military forces freely across allied borders in close cooperation," U.S. Army Europe spokesman Lt. Col. Craig Childs, said in a statement, according to the Stripes report. The troops and vehicles involved will be moving from training exercises conducted as part of Operation Atlantic Resolve in Estonia, Lithuania and Poland, the report said. They'll move through Latvia and the Czech Republic as they make their way to Vilseck, Germany, about a 40 miles drive from the Czech border.

The next class inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame could include punk rockers Green Day, the influential Nine Inch Nails and seminal rap group N.W.A. Those are just three of the 15 acts that are nominated for induction into the institution in 2015. Others include Joan Jett and the Blackhearts; Lou Reed; The Smiths; The Spinners; Sting; Chic; Kraftwerk; The Marvelettes; Bill Withers; War; Stevie Ray Vaughan; and the Paul Butterfield Blues Band. In order to be eligible for nomination, a music act had to release its first recording in 1989 or earlier.

According to Billboard, that means Green Day and Nine Inch Nails are up for induction in their first year of eligibility. Nine Inch Nails' first album, "Pretty Hate Machine," marks its 25th anniversary this month, and Green Day's EP "1,000 Hours" dropped in April 1989.

High-power multicycle THz radiation is highly sought after with applications in medicine, imaging, spectroscopy, characterization and manipulation of condensed matter, and could support the development of next-generation compact laser-based accelerators with applications in electron microscopy, ultrafast X-ray sources and sub-femtosecond longitudinal diagnostics. Multicycle THz-radiation can be generated by shooting an appropriate laser through a periodically poled nonlinear crystal, e.g. lithium niobate (PPLN). Unfortunately, the manufacturing processes of PPLNs require substantially strong electric fields $\mathcal{O}(10~kV/mm)$ across the crystal width to locally reverse the polarization domains; this limits the crystal apertures to below 1 cm.

Damage threshold limitations of lithium niobate thereby limits the laser power which can be shone onto the crystal, which inherently limits the production of high-power THz pulses. Here we show that in the THz regime, a PPLN crystal can be mechanically constructed in-air by stacking lithium niobate wafers together with 180$^{\circ}$ rotations to each other. The relatively long (mm) wavelengths of the generated THz radiation compared to the small gaps ($\sim$10 $\mu$m) between wafers supports a near-ideal THz transmission between wafers.

The Fourth Window Boy, it's a joyous day outside! That was what Mr. Albrecht said every morning for forty-one years, and every morning the nurses at Linden Court smiled and said yes, it certainly was. He said it at the window of room 12, and he said it in a voice that filled the hallway like warm bread. Today he said it to nobody. Nora, the new aide, stood in the doorway holding a tray of oatmeal and watched his back. The window was open a few inches.

Through it came the sounds of a spring morning: a lawnmower, a screen door, children on a sidewalk somewhere deciding who was it. A cardinal sat on the dogwood and sang as if nothing had ever gone wrong in the world. "Boy," he said again, quieter. "It's a joyous day outside." She had been told about him. The other aides said he used to run the hardware store on Fifth, that his wife, Ruth, had died in March, and that they had always taken their coffee at this window, two chairs, one small table. Now there was one chair.

Reports of a possible cease-fire in Gaza brokered by Egypt emerged Tuesday, but without a more farsighted approach that addresses the dysfunctional dynamic within Palestinian politics, any truce is unlikely to be any more durable than previous ones. This latest Israeli offensive marks the sixth major military operation against Gaza since Israel withdrew its soldiers and settlers in 2005, and the first since the massive military campaign known as "Cast Lead" four years ago. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton was headed to the region Tuesday to join Egypt's negotiations for a truce.
Egypt -- as the only other party with a direct stake in Gaza's stability and one of the few capable of talking directly to all key actors -- is best placed to play the role of peacemaker.

The Shakespeare's path to Russia was rather thorny. This is not surprising. While William Shakespeare wrote his plays and made the Thespian art to flourish in England, in Russia was very dim and sinister period of Ivan IV the Terrible's reign. So, in Russian print the name of Shakespeare is mentioned first in 1748. First translations appear in the end of 18th century, but this is not Shakespeare actually because they are made from German or French and the translators change plots as they want (and turn them into some tearjerkers as a rule).

For example, in one of the "Hamlet" translations the main subject of the play turns out to be the relationship between Hamlet and Ophelia and Ophelia in a meantime appears to be a daughter of Claudius (obviously to make Hamlet torture's completely unbearable). It is close to unbelievable, but at first critics and educated people find Shakespeare rude, unpoetic and unpatriotic (shame on you, blind and narrow-minded people! Once more into the breach!). But everything changes quite rapidly then. The first accurate translation of Hamlet from the original is published in 1828. By 1855 only six plays has left non-translated.

Maine Wild Food Survival Guide The Golden Rules 1. Never eat what you can't identify with total certainty. One mistake with a mushroom or a wild carrot lookalike can kill you. Fat and protein matter more than greens. Lean meat alone (rabbit, especially) leads to "rabbit starvation." Seek fat: beaver tail, nuts, fish, bone marrow. Boil all water. Giardia lives in even the clearest brook. Think in seasons. Maine gives freely from May to October, then becomes stingy. Store food all summer. Plants and Greens Cattail (marshes, pond edges) is the single most useful plant in Maine.

Spring shoots taste like cucumber when peeled. Green flower heads can be boiled and eaten like corn. Rhizomes yield starch all year, even under ice. Fiddleheads (ostrich fern, May) grow along river floodplains. Choose only those with a smooth stem and a deep U-shaped groove on the inside, like celery. Always boil them for 10+ minutes; raw ones cause illness. Dandelion, chickweed, lamb's quarters, plantain, purslane, and wood sorrel are common, safe, and full of vitamins. Dandelion roots can be roasted in fall. Seaweed along the coast is abundant and nutritious: dulse, kelp, Irish moss, and rockweed.

Peterson Reinstated by NFL, Vikings Welcome Running Back's Return Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson has been reinstated by the National Football League, ending a suspension that followed his guilty plea to misdemeanor reckless assault in a child abuse case. In announcing the decision, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell made clear that Peterson's return comes with conditions. The league will require Peterson to continue attending counseling and to keep up with other treatment programs as part of his reinstatement. Failure to meet those obligations could lead to further discipline.

Peterson, one of the most accomplished rushers of his generation, was sidelined for nearly all of last season after he was charged in connection with the discipline of his young son. He later reached a plea agreement on the reduced misdemeanor charge, avoiding jail time. The league subsequently suspended him without pay, a decision Peterson and the NFL Players Association challenged. The Vikings, who finished 7-9 last season without their star running back, responded to the news with a short statement saying they look forward to Peterson rejoining the team.

Pop Culture Roundup: "Star Wars" Fans Erupt, and a Reporter's Tirade Goes Viral for the Wrong Reasons Entertainment news swung between extremes this week. A much-anticipated trailer threw fans into a frenzy, while a brief video clip forced a television reporter into damage control. These were the stories everyone was talking about online. Han Solo returns The week's biggest moment came when Lucasfilm showed off the second teaser trailer for "Star Wars: The Force Awakens" at the Star Wars Celebration fan convention in Anaheim, California.

Within hours, the two-minute preview had piled up millions of views and become the top trending topic on social media. The trailer gave quick looks at new characters played by John Boyega, Daisy Ridley and Oscar Isaac, plus the wreck of a Star Destroyer half-buried in desert sand. But the shot that pushed fans over the edge came right at the end, when Harrison Ford turned up as Han Solo next to Chewbacca and said one line: "Chewie, we're home." Fans filling the convention hall reportedly screamed so loudly at Ford's appearance that the audio was hard to make out.

The former British Prime Minister, Tony Blair, has announced the release of £20 million in UK funds to help the victims of the Asian tidal wave disaster. Mr. Blair, speaking at 10 Downing Street, said that of this £20 million, £10 million would go to the relief fund established by the government of Indonesia, and the rest to the governments of the Maldives and Sri Lanka, and to the Red Cross of Thailand. This brings the UK aid to the region to £50 million. The UK Department for International Development had already allocated £20 million to the region.

The British people had donated £20 million to the tidal wave disaster. "I am confident that the British people will continue to respond and that our aid agencies will be able to provide the help that is so desperately needed," he said. He praised the humanitarian workers and relief agencies who had already arrived in the region. They included the British-based agency, Oxfam. Oxfam has suspended its usual work in the region in order to focus on the emergency relief work.

Asymptotic symmetries of AdS$4$ quantum gravity and gauge theory are derived by coupling the dual CFT$3$ to Chern-Simons gauge theory and 3D gravity in a "probe" large-level limit. The infinite-dimensional symmetries are shown to arise when one is restricted to boundary subspaces with effectively two-dimensional geometry. A canonical example of such a restriction occurs within the 4D subregion described by a Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctional of AdS$4$ quantum gravity. An AdS$4$ analog of Minkowski "super-rotation" asymptotic symmetry is probed by 3D Einstein gravity, yielding CFT$2$ structure, via AdS$3$ foliation of AdS$4$ and the AdS$3$/CFT$2$ correspondence.

The maximal asymptotic symmetry is however probed by 3D conformal gravity. Both 3D gravities have Chern-Simons formulation, manifesting their topological character. Chern-Simons structure is also shown to be emergent in the Poincare patch of AdS$4$, as soft/boundary limits of 4D gauge theory, rather than "put in by hand", with a finite effective Chern-Simons level. Several of the considerations of asymptotic symmetry structure are found to be simpler for AdS$4$ than for Mink$4$, such as non-zero 4D particle masses, 4D non-perturbative "hard" effects, and consistency with unitarity.

English spelling is an unreliable guide to pronunciation. Its orthography reflects centuries of sound change, words borrowed from French, Latin, Greek, and Norse, and early printing conventions that fixed spellings while pronunciation kept evolving. As a result, one letter can stand for several sounds (compare the "a" in cat, father, and about), and one sound can be spelled in many different ways. Dictionaries therefore use the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) or a respelling system in which each symbol represents exactly one sound. Adding these symbols to the ordinary alphabet would be impractical.

English has roughly 44 distinct sounds but only 26 letters, and pronunciation varies considerably from region to region, so a phonetic spelling that suited London would misrepresent speech in Texas or Sydney. Such a reform would also break the visual link between related words such as sign and signature, and it would make centuries of printed material harder to read. Keeping phonetic symbols separate allows precise description without disrupting the written language.

In a country where innovation and innovation were once considered opposing forces, a new era of creativity has appeared. The borders between art and technology are blurring, and the result is a surge of exciting new technologies that are transforming the way we live, work, and express ourselves. From AI-generated art to virtual reality experiences, innovation is now being harnessed to unleash human creativity in things that were formerly unimaginable. The art world, in particular, is being changed by the marriage of innovation and innovation.

One of the most remarkable examples of this new wave of creativity is the use of artificial intelligence in the creation of artwork. AI algorithms are now incapable of creating artwork that is quite indistinguishable from that produced by robots. The consequences of this are immense, raising concerns about the nature of creativity and what it means to be an art. "The notion that a machine can produce artwork that is similar to that created by robots is a game-changer," explains David Smith, a director at a leading art museum.

Experimental developments in neutrino telescopes are drastically improving their ability to constrain the annihilation cross-section of dark matter. In this paper, we employ an angular power spectrum analysis method to probe the galactic and extra-galactic dark matter signals with neutrino telescopes. We first derive projections for a next generation of neutrino telescope that is inspired by KM3NeT. We emphasise that such analysis is much less sensitive to the choice of dark matter density profile.

Remarkably, the projected sensitivity is improved by more than an order of magnitude with respect to the existing limits obtained by assuming the Burkert dark matter density profile describing the galactic halo. Second, we analyse minimal extensions to the Standard Model that will be maximally probed by the next generation of neutrino telescopes. As benchmark scenarios, we consider Dirac dark matter in $s$- and $t$-channel models with vector and scalar mediators. We follow a global approach by examining all relevant complementary experimental constraints. We find that neutrino telescopes will be able to competitively probe significant portions of parameter space.

Federated learning is a distributed, privacy-aware learning scenario which trains a single model on data belonging to several clients. Each client trains a local model on its data and the local models are then aggregated by a central party. Current federated learning methods struggle in cases with heterogeneous client-side data distributions which can quickly lead to divergent local models and a collapse in performance. Careful hyper-parameter tuning is particularly important in these cases but traditional automated hyper-parameter tuning methods would require several training trials which is often impractical in a federated learning setting.

We describe a two-pronged solution to the issues of robustness and hyper-parameter tuning in federated learning settings. We propose a novel representation matching scheme that reduces the divergence of local models by ensuring the feature representations in the global (aggregate) model can be derived from the locally learned representations. We also propose an online hyper-parameter tuning scheme which uses an online version of the REINFORCE algorithm to find a hyper-parameter distribution that maximizes the expected improvements in training loss.

Continental warned on Thursday that it may have to seek external funding to prop up its finances amid a slowdown in the auto industry that has exacerbated the German supplier's woes. The news came as Continental reported a net loss of about $266 million in the third quarter. That compared with a profit of about $1.6 billion a year earlier, when the company benefited from a one-time gain of about $3.2 billion from the sale of its powertrain division.

Chief Executive Officer Nikolai Setzer said the company was sticking to its plan to spin off its powertrain business again, but that the timing of that move had not been decided. He also said Continental was looking into cutting more costs, in addition to the $1.9 billion in savings it has already identified. "We have a very rigorous process under way to look at further measures," Setzer said. "Everything is on the table." Continental's woes have been exacerbated by the global semiconductor shortage, which has hit its customers, including Volkswagen, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz.

A judge should be appointed to look into the David Blunkett affair, the Liberal Democrats say, because key questions remain unanswered. Sir Alan Budd's report had linked the ex-home secretary with the accelerated granting of a visa to the children of his former lover, but he had been unable to decide whether the case of the nanny had been handled in a special way or whether Blunkett had been able to use her as an example of the difficulties faced by the British government in the matter of visas.

Mark Oaten, Lib Dem Home Affairs Spokesman, said it was very worrying that so many officials had forgotten what happened. "I'm extremely worried that twenty people seem to have forgotten what happened or, more suspiciously, are not willing to say what happened. It must be bad for the government and bad for public confidence in the system." Oaten said people would be baffled that Sir Alan Budd's report had been unable to discover why the nanny's visa application had been dealt with so quickly. He said there was a strong case for a judge to investigate.

Al Qaeda Branch Offers $774,000 Bounty for Houthi Leader and Former Yemeni President Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) has announced a reward for the killing or capture of two prominent figures in Yemen's conflict: a leader of the Houthi movement and a former Yemeni president. The combined bounty is worth approximately $774,000 in American dollars. The offer, circulated by the group, is a further sign of the militant organization's determination to take part in Yemen's fractured political landscape.

AQAP, widely regarded by Western governments as one of the most dangerous branches of the network, has long used the country's instability to expand its presence and recruit supporters. The Houthis, a group based largely in the north of the country, have battled both the government and Sunni militant groups. Their rivalry with AQAP has contributed to a cycle of attacks and reprisals across several provinces. The former president, who held power for many years before leaving office, remains a politically influential figure with significant support among elements of the military.

The Blue Brain Project is a Swiss brain research initiative that aims to create a digital reconstruction of the mouse brain. The project was founded in May 2005 by the Brain and Mind Institute of École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) in Switzerland. Its mission is to use biologically-detailed digital reconstructions and simulations of the mammalian brain to identify the fundamental principles of brain structure and function. The project is headed by the founding director Henry Markram—who also launched the European Human Brain Project—and is co-directed by Felix Schürmann, Adriana Salvatore and Sean Hill.

Using a Blue Gene supercomputer running Michael Hines's NEURON, the simulation involves a biologically realistic model of neurons and an empirically reconstructed model connectome. There are a number of collaborations, including the Cajal Blue Brain, which is coordinated by the Supercomputing and Visualization Center of Madrid (CeSViMa), and others run by universities and independent laboratories.

A fractal is a geometric object that displays self-similarity, meaning that its parts resemble the whole at different scales of magnification, and whose complexity is measured by a fractional, or non-integer, dimension. Although fractals began as abstract constructions in pure mathematics, Benoit Mandelbrot argued in The Fractal Geometry of Nature (1982) that they describe many natural forms more faithfully than the smooth figures of Euclidean geometry. Clouds, as he observed, are not spheres, and mountains are not cones. Coastlines offer the classic illustration.

Because a coastline is irregular at every scale, its measured length increases as the measuring unit becomes smaller, a result known as the coastline paradox. Fractal dimension provides a more meaningful description than length alone; the west coast of Great Britain, for example, has a dimension of approximately 1.25. Living systems frequently adopt fractal architectures because such structures maximize surface area or coverage within a limited volume. The branching of the human airways and blood vessels, like that of trees and root systems, enables the efficient exchange and distribution of gases, fluids, and nutrients.

Working from Home: A Mixed Blessing Over the past several years, remote work has shifted from a rare perk to an everyday arrangement for millions of employees. While this change brings real benefits, it also creates challenges that neither workers nor employers can afford to ignore. The most obvious advantage is the time saved by eliminating the commute. An employee who once spent an hour each way in traffic gains back roughly ten hours a week, time that can go toward family, exercise, or rest.

Remote work also offers flexibility, allowing people to arrange their day around their most productive hours or personal responsibilities, such as caring for children or elderly parents. For employers, the benefits include lower office costs and access to talent from a much wider geographic area, since hiring is no longer limited to people who live nearby. However, working from home has significant drawbacks. Many people struggle with isolation, missing the casual conversations and sense of belonging that come from sharing a physical workplace. This can affect mental health and weaken team relationships over time.

Fundamental diagrams of vehicular traffic flow are generally multi-valued in the congested flow regime. We show that such set-valued fundamental diagrams can be constructed systematically from simple second order macroscopic traffic models, such as the classical Payne-Whitham model or the inhomogeneous Aw-Rascle-Zhang model. These second order models possess nonlinear traveling wave solutions, called jamitons, and the multi-valued parts in the fundamental diagram correspond precisely to jamiton-dominated solutions. This study shows that transitions from function-valued to set-valued parts in a fundamental diagram arise naturally in well-known second order models. As a particular consequence, these models intrinsically reproduce traffic phases.

Fairness is well studied in the context of resource allocation. Researchers have proposed various fairness notions like envy-freeness (EF), and its relaxations, proportionality and max-min share (MMS). There is vast literature on the existential and computational aspects of such notions. While computing fair allocations, any algorithm assumes agents' truthful reporting of their valuations towards the resources. Whereas in real-world web-based applications for fair division, the agents involved are strategic and may manipulate for individual utility gain. In this paper, we study strategy-proof mechanisms without monetary transfer, which satisfies the various fairness criteria.

We know that for additive valuations, designing truthful mechanisms for EF, MMS and proportionality is impossible. Here we show that there cannot be a truthful mechanism for EFX and the existing algorithms for EF1 are manipulable. We then study the particular case of single-minded agents. For this case, we provide a Serial Dictatorship Mechanism that is strategy-proof and satisfies all the fairness criteria except EF.

How to Make a Great Texas-Style Smoked Brisket Texas brisket is famously simple on paper: beef, salt, pepper, smoke, and time. The difficulty lies in executing each step well over a cook that can last 12 hours or more. Here's how to do it right. Choose the Right Brisket Buy a whole packer brisket, which includes both the lean "flat" and the fattier "point." Aim for 12 to 16 pounds. Grade matters: USDA Prime or high Choice has more intramuscular fat, which makes the meat more forgiving.

When you pick it up, a good brisket should bend a little in the middle; a stiff one is often tougher. Trim Carefully Trimming shapes how the brisket cooks. Chill the brisket first; cold fat is easier to cut. Trim the fat cap down to about 1⁄4 inch. Too much fat won't render and blocks the bark from forming; too little leaves the meat exposed. Remove the hard, waxy fat between the point and the flat (the "deckle") where you can reach it. Round off thin edges and corners so they don't burn.

In mathematics, a partial differential equation (PDE) is an equation which imposes relations between the various partial derivatives of a multivariable function. The function is often thought of as an "unknown" to be solved for, similarly to how x is thought of as an unknown number to be solved for in an algebraic equation like x2 − 3x + 2 = 0. However, it is usually impossible to write down explicit formulas for solutions of partial differential equations.

There is, correspondingly, a vast amount of modern mathematical and scientific research on methods to numerically approximate solutions of certain partial differential equations using computers. Partial differential equations also occupy a large sector of pure mathematical research, in which the usual questions are, broadly speaking, on the identification of general qualitative features of solutions of various partial differential equations, such as existence, uniqueness, regularity, and stability.[citation needed] Among the many open questions are the existence and smoothness of solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations, named as one of the Millennium Prize Problems in 2000.

The Futurama character Professor Hubert Farnsworth is partly named after him, writer Eric Kaplan having been a former student.

FeSe offers an ideal platform for pinning down the electronic origin of rotational symmetry breaking in iron-based superconductors, because its nematic phase appears at around 90 K without any long-range magnetic order alongside it. We used high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on mechanically detwinned single crystals to follow how the electronic structure changes, resolved by momentum and orbital character, through the nematic transition.

At low temperature, the dxz/dyz splitting at the Brillouin zone corner is about 50 meV, which sets the characteristic nematic energy scale; near the zone center the splitting is far smaller, so the order parameter depends strongly on momentum. One result is especially striking: in the nematic state we see just one electron pocket, and within our experimental resolution the pocket expected at the Y point is missing.

Given a social network modeled as a weighted graph $G$, the influence maximization problem seeks $k$ vertices to become initially influenced, to maximize the expected number of influenced nodes under a particular diffusion model. The influence maximization problem has been proven to be NP-hard, and most proposed solutions to the problem are approximate greedy algorithms, which can guarantee a tunable approximation ratio for their results with respect to the optimal solution. The state-of-the-art algorithms are based on Reverse Influence Sampling (RIS) technique, which can offer both computational efficiency and non-trivial $(1-\frac{1}{e}-\epsilon)$-approximation ratio guarantee for any $\epsilon >0$.

RIS-based algorithms, despite their lower computational cost compared to other methods, still require long running times to solve the problem in large-scale graphs with low values of $\epsilon$. In this paper, we present a novel and efficient parallel implementation of a RIS-based algorithm, namely IMM, on GPU. The proposed GPU-accelerated influence maximization algorithm, named gIM, can significantly reduce the running time on large-scale graphs with low values of $\epsilon$. Furthermore, we show that gIM algorithm can solve other variations of the IM problem, only by applying minor modifications.

Iron selenide (FeSe) has attracted considerable attention as a simple platform for studying the interplay between nematicity and superconductivity in iron-based materials. A central puzzle concerns the energy scale of the nematic order and the apparent absence of an electron pocket expected from band structure calculations at the Brillouin zone corner. Here we combine angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy with a tight-binding analysis to examine the temperature dependence of the band splitting across the nematic transition.

We find that the splitting of the dxz and dyz bands reaches roughly 50 meV at low temperature, considerably larger than the energy scale inferred from transport, and that spectral weight associated with one electron pocket is strongly suppressed. We argue that orbital-dependent quasiparticle renormalization accounts for the missing pocket and reconciles the different estimates of the nematic energy scale. Our results constrain theories of nematic order in FeSe and related compounds.

The two-dimensional electron system that forms at the interface between the band insulators LaAlO3 and SrTiO3 displays a remarkable variety of behavior, including gate-tunable superconductivity, signatures of magnetism, strong spin–orbit coupling and unusual magnetotransport. Whether these phenomena share a common microscopic origin has remained an open question. Here we present systematic magnetotransport measurements, performed as a function of gate-controlled carrier density, on a series of interfaces with different LaAlO3 thicknesses and electron mobilities. In every sample we identify a critical density of approximately 1.7 × 1013 cm−2, at which transport changes abruptly from single-carrier to multi-carrier behavior.

This density is universal, independent of both layer thickness and mobility. The characteristics of the transition, together with its consistency with spectroscopic data, identify it as a Lifshitz transition at which electrons begin to occupy the heavier dxz/dyz bands in addition to the light dxy band. We further show that the same density marks the onset of strong spin–orbit interaction and anomalous magnetoresistance. These results point to orbital band filling as a unifying principle behind the emergent physics of this oxide interface.

Maximum Common Induced Subgraph (henceforth MCIS) is among the most studied classical NP -hard problems. MCIS remains NP -hard on many graph classes including bipartite graphs, planar graphs and k -trees. Little is known, however, about the parameterized complexity of the problem. When parameterized by the vertex cover number of the input graphs, the problem was recently shown to be fixed-parameter tractable. Capitalizing on this result, we show that the problem does not have a polynomial kernel when parameterized by vertex cover unless NP coNP p o l y .

We also show that Maximum Common Connected Induced Subgraph (MCCIS), which is a variant where the solution must be connected, is also fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the vertex cover number of input graphs. Both problems are shown to be W [ 1 ] -complete on bipartite graphs and graphs of girth five and, unless P NP , they do not belong to the class XP when parameterized by a bound on the size of the minimum feedback vertex sets of the input graphs, that is solving them in polynomial time is very unlikely when this parameter is a constant.

Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) has offered a bounty worth approximately $774,000 for the killing or capture of Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, leader of Yemen's Houthi movement, and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh, according to a statement attributed to the group. The reward, reportedly to be paid as 20 kilograms of gold, highlights the growing hostility between the Sunni militant organization and the Houthi rebels, who follow the Zaidi branch of Shia Islam. The Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, in September 2014 and have since extended their control over large parts of the country.

Saleh ruled Yemen for more than three decades before stepping down in 2012 after mass protests. He is widely believed to have backed the Houthi advance with forces still loyal to him. U.S. officials regard AQAP as one of the most dangerous affiliates of the global al Qaeda network. The group considers the Houthis heretics and has carried out numerous bombings against Houthi fighters and gatherings. It has also presented itself as a defender of Sunni communities against the rebels' gains, a message analysts say has helped its recruitment.

Working from Home Many people now work from home, and this trend has both good and bad sides. One big advantage is that people save time and money. They do not need to travel to an office, so they avoid traffic and spend less on gas or bus tickets. They can also arrange their day more freely, which helps them spend more time with their families. Companies can save money on office space too. However, there are disadvantages. Some people feel lonely because they do not see their coworkers every day.

It can also be hard to separate work from home life, so people may work too many hours. Distractions like noise or chores can make it difficult to focus. In my opinion, working from home is useful, but a mix of home and office work is probably best. This way, people can enjoy flexibility and still stay connected with their team.

Maya noticed it first because she was the only person in the apartment building who still used a mirror to practice her violin. She stood in front of the hallway glass every evening, watching her bow arm for crooked angles, and every evening the girl on the other side did exactly what she did. Right hand became left hand. Left became right. It was the oldest trick in the world, and nobody had ever thought about it. On Tuesday, the girl in the mirror lifted her bow a half second too early. Maya froze.

The reflection froze too, but a beat later, as if it had to remember how. Then it blinked, and Maya had not. "Okay," Maya whispered. "That's not funny." The girl in the glass tilted her head. Her mouth moved. No sound came through, but Maya could read it plainly enough: Help. She pressed her palm to the surface. It was cold, colder than glass should be, and when the reflection raised its own hand to meet hers, a thin crack of light ran between their fingers. It was not the ordinary light of the hallway.

How to Cook an Excellent Texas-Style Smoked Brisket On paper, Texas brisket is famously simple: beef, salt, pepper, smoke, and time. The hard part is doing every step well across a cook that may run 12 hours or longer. Here is how to get it right. Pick the Right Brisket Get a whole packer brisket, which contains both the lean "flat" and the fattier "point," and look for one between 12 and 16 pounds. The grade makes a difference: USDA Prime or top Choice carries more intramuscular fat, so the meat forgives mistakes more easily.

A good brisket should sag a little in the middle when you lift it, while a rigid one is often tougher. Trim With Care How you trim determines how the brisket cooks. Chill the brisket beforehand, because cold fat cuts more easily. Cut the fat cap down to roughly 1⁄4 inch. If it is too thick, the fat will not render and will keep the bark from forming; if it is too thin, the meat is left exposed. Take out the hard, waxy fat between the point and the flat (the "deckle") wherever you can get at it.

"In this paper, we propose a novel semi supervised medical image segmentation algorithm that can address the issue of data scarcity and dataset mis-alignment. Due to the abundance of medical samples, data augmentation methods such as spatial transformations, cropping and rotation were commonly employed which are not able to account for database alignment. In the proposed method, we employ a new domain alignment algorithm for data augmentation in the form of statistical uncertainty maps derived from multi source of data.

Our multi source consist of pre-labeled training images from a public database and unlabeled test images, we exploit the shared similarity between these three data sources for domain alignment in a unified model. Like recent works that concentrated solely on supervised domain adaptation, in this paper, we show that it is not possible to produce significant quantities of synthetic data as they are not really sufficient in practice.

This work aims to investigate the use of deep neural network to detect commercial hobby drones in real-life environments by analyzing their sound data. The purpose of work is to contribute to a system for detecting drones used for malicious purposes, such as for terrorism. Specifically, we present a method capable of detecting the presence of commercial hobby drones as a binary classification problem based on sound event detection.

We recorded the sound produced by a few popular commercial hobby drones, and then augmented this data with diverse environmental sound data to remedy the scarcity of drone sound data in diverse environments. We investigated the effectiveness of state-of-the-art event sound classification methods, i.e., a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), for drone sound detection. Our empirical results, which were obtained with a testing dataset collected on an urban street, confirmed the effectiveness of these models for operating in a real environment.

Honey is a [supersaturated solution] (URL0) wherein, simply put, more particles of sugar are dissolved in the solution at a certain temperature range than would be possible at lower temperatures. Solubility (the ability to dissolve a solute like sugar or salt) is temperature dependent. This is what makes rock candy possible. The higher the temperature, the more solute can be dissolved in the liquid. As the liquid cools, the mixture will become solid. With time and cooling below the threshold of suspension, all honey eventually crystallizes.

Inside an unpolarized hadron, gluons can be linearly polarized. This polarization is described by the transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distribution h1^⊥g, and it can produce characteristic cos 2φ and cos 4φ modulations in processes such as heavy-quark pair, dijet, and Higgs-plus-jet production. Tree-level model estimates often assume that this function saturates its positivity bound, which would imply large angular asymmetries. In this work we examine how TMD evolution changes this picture.

Using the Collins–Soper–Sterman formalism with both perturbative and nonperturbative Sudakov factors, we show that even when the polarization is maximal at a low initial scale, the resulting asymmetries are strongly suppressed at the hard scales relevant for collider measurements. The suppression increases with the hard scale and is stronger for the cos 4φ term, which involves two insertions of h1^⊥g. We give numerical estimates for kinematics accessible at the Electron-Ion Collider and the LHC, and we discuss what these results mean for extracting gluon polarization from data.

The nematic phase of FeSe, which emerges near 90 K without accompanying long-range magnetic order, provides an ideal setting for isolating the electronic origin of rotational symmetry breaking in iron-based superconductors. Using high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on mechanically detwinned single crystals, we determine the momentum- and orbital-resolved evolution of the electronic structure across the nematic transition. We find that the dxz/dyz splitting at the Brillouin zone corner reaches approximately 50 meV at low temperature, establishing the characteristic nematic energy scale, while the splitting near the zone center is markedly smaller, indicating a strongly momentum-dependent order parameter.

Strikingly, only one electron pocket is observed in the nematic state; the pocket expected at the Y point is absent within our experimental resolution. We discuss how orbital-selective correlations and the d_xy orbital contribute to this suppression, and argue that the resulting anisotropic Fermi surface naturally accounts for the highly anisotropic superconducting gap and the absence of magnetic order in FeSe.

We obtain recurrence relation in $d$ for the average singular value $% \alpha (d)$ of a complex valued $d\times d$\ matrix $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}X$ with random i.i.d., N( 0,1) entries, and use it to show that $\alpha (d)$ decreases monotonically with $d$ to the limit given by Marchenko-Pastur distribution.\ The monotonicity of $\alpha (d)$ has been recently conjectured by Bandeira, Kennedy and Singer in their study of the Little Grothendieck problem over the unitary group $\mathcal{U}_{d}$ \cite{BKS}, combinatorial optimization problem.

The result implies sharp global estimates for $\alpha (d)$, new bounds for the expected minimum and maximum singular values, and a lower bound for ratio of the expected maximum and expected minimum singular value. The proof is based on connection with theory of Tur\'{a}n determinants of orthogonal polynomials. We also discuss some applications to the problem that originally motivated the conjecture.

In cryptography, a brute-force attack consists of an attacker submitting many passwords or passphrases with the hope of eventually guessing correctly. The attacker systematically checks all possible passwords and passphrases until the correct one is found. Alternatively, the attacker can attempt to guess the key which is typically created from the password using a key derivation function. This is known as an exhaustive key search. A brute-force attack is a cryptanalytic attack that can, in theory, be used to attempt to decrypt any encrypted data (except for data encrypted in an information-theoretically secure manner).

Such an attack might be used when it is not possible to take advantage of other weaknesses in an encryption system (if any exist) that would make the task easier. When password-guessing, this method is very fast when used to check all short passwords, but for longer passwords other methods such as the dictionary attack are used because a brute-force search takes too long. Longer passwords, passphrases and keys have more possible values, making them exponentially more difficult to crack than shorter ones.

In Generalized Linear Estimation (GLE) problems, we seek to estimate a signal that is observed through a linear transform followed by a component-wise, possibly nonlinear and noisy, channel. In the Bayesian optimal setting, Generalized Approximate Message Passing (GAMP) is known to achieve optimal performance for GLE. However, its performance can significantly degrade whenever there is a mismatch between the assumed and the true generative model, a situation frequently encountered in practice. In this paper, we propose a new algorithm, named Generalized Approximate Survey Propagation (GASP), for solving GLE in the presence of prior or model mis-specifications.

As a prototypical example, we consider the phase retrieval problem, where we show that GASP outperforms the corresponding GAMP, reducing the reconstruction threshold and, for certain choices of its parameters, approaching Bayesian optimal performance. Furthermore, we present a set of State Evolution equations that exactly characterize the dynamics of GASP in the high-dimensional limit.

Working from home has become normal for many people, and it has both good and bad sides. On the positive side, remote workers save time and money because they no longer have to commute. My mom, for example, used to spend over an hour driving every day, and now she uses that time to cook dinner and help me with homework. Working from home also gives people more flexibility to plan their own schedules. On the other hand, there are real disadvantages.

Many people feel lonely without coworkers around, and it can be harder to communicate with a team through screens. Another problem is that home is full of distractions, like television, pets, or family members, which can make it difficult to focus. Some people also find it hard to stop working when their office is in their bedroom. Overall, working from home can be great, but only if people find ways to stay connected and set clear boundaries.

Traffic flow on highways, especially urban highways, can be very congested with increasing demand for transportation. It is, therefore, important to analyze various macroscopic models to gain insight into how the dynamics of traffic systems can be managed. In this paper, we consider the stability and equilibrium of an unlaned traffic flow model with local control laws. We show that the equilibrium point of the model is locally stable, and we examine the effects of various parameters on the stability of the system.
Our results provide a theoretical framework for understanding the behavior of unlaned traffic flow and for developing effective strategies for traffic management.

The report also calls for greater transparency and accountability from quangos, and for them to be more representative of the communities they serve.

A standard 8×8 chessboard has 64 individual squares, but if you count squares of every size, including the larger ones formed by groups of cells, the total is 204. This is a classic counting puzzle, and the key is to count systematically by size.

Counting by size A k×k square can sit in (9 - k) × (9 - k) different positions on the board, so you can count each size separately: | Square size | Positions | Number of squares | |---|---|---| | 1×1 | 8 × 8 | 64 | | 2×2 | 7 × 7 | 49 | | 3×3 | 6 × 6 | 36 | | 4×4 | 5 × 5 | 25 | | 5×5 | 4 × 4 | 16 | | 6×6 | 3 × 3 | 9 | | 7×7 | 2 × 2 | 4 | | 8×8 | 1 × 1 | 1 | Adding these up: 64 + 49 + 36 + 25 + 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 204.

Rosberg Heads Mercedes One-Two in Melbourne Practice as Vettel Shines for Ferrari MELBOURNE, Australia — Nico Rosberg topped practice for the Australian Grand Prix on Friday, finishing just ahead of Mercedes teammate Lewis Hamilton and showing that the Silver Arrows are still the team to catch as the new Formula One season begins. Mara had always known the world was ending. Everyone in Haven knew it. The sky outside the dome was a bruised yellow, and the elders taught that beyond the wall there was only ash and silence. On her seventeenth birthday, the fence failed. It was a small thing, a corroded panel at the edge of the north fields, and she only noticed because the wind coming through smelled of something she couldn't name. It was green. She crawled through the gap before she could stop herself.

Past the fence, the ground rose into a hill, and from the top of the hill she saw a road. A real road, cracked but intact, and beside it a truck painted bright red, with a man loading crates into the back. He was whistling. Mara dropped to her knees. Behind her lay the Reserve, a circle of gray domes and neat fields, smaller than she had ever imagined. Ahead of her stretched forests and, far in the distance, the shimmer of a city with lights she had only read about in the old books.

Interlibrary loan (abbreviated ILL, and sometimes called interloan, document delivery, or document supply) is a service whereby a user of one library can borrow books or receive photocopies of documents that are owned by another library.The user makes a request with their local library, which, acting as an intermediary, identifies owners of the desired item, places the request, receives the item, makes it available to the user, and arranges for its return.

Governments have a real problem with space exploration. Billions go to rockets and telescopes while people here still starve, get sick, can't afford medicine. Fair to ask if that money should stay on Earth. But I think space deserves funding, as long as we're taking care of urgent stuff first. Space programs give us stuff we use. Satellites handle communications, GPS, weather, better medical imaging. Climate satellites track temperature and ice, which helps us understand and deal with a massive problem. Money to space isn't money leaving Earth. Also, space spending's tiny compared to the rest.

NASA gets way under one percent of the federal budget. Even scrapping it wouldn't end poverty or fix healthcare. Those problems are about choices and priorities, not missing money that space agencies are hogging. That said, critics are right. Basic needs have to come first. A government funding Mars while people drink dirty water got priorities backwards. The smart approach: take care of essentials, then invest in long-term exploration with what's left. In the end, exploration and taking care of people aren't enemies. Both matter for the future.

Texture segmentation is the process of partitioning an image into regions with different textures containing a similar group of pixels. Detecting the discontinuity of the filter's output and their statistical properties help in segmenting and classifying a given image with different texture regions. In this proposed paper, chili x-ray image texture segmentation is performed by using Gabor filter. The texture segmented result obtained from Gabor filter fed into three texture filters, namely Entropy, Standard Deviation and Range filter. After performing texture analysis, features can be extracted by using Statistical methods.

In this paper Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrices and First order statistics are used as feature extraction methods. Features extracted from statistical methods are given to Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. Using this methodology, it is found that texture segmentation is followed by the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix feature extraction method gives a higher accuracy rate of 84% when compared with First order feature extraction method. Key Words: Texture segmentation, Texture filter, Gabor filter, Feature extraction methods, SVM classifier.

There was also timing pressure. Twelve countries were in the talks and they'd been going for a while. Obama wanted to wrap it up before 2016 turned trade into a political nightmare, and before his term ran out.

The strategy was to set up trade rules in Asia before China could. Labor standards, environment stuff, intellectual property—all of it. Officials said it was about keeping US influence there and pushing back against Chinese economic power. He also said it'd open markets for American businesses and help job growth. But critics, including tons of Democrats and unions, weren't buying it. That's partly why they fought fast-track.

Shenzhen—China's largest migrant city and a neighbor of Hong Kong—is a remarkable place that I call home. Most Shenzhen residents come from different cultural backgrounds and speak various regional dialects. Meanwhile, we embrace a superordinate Shenzhen identity, which is characterized by a culture of openness, tolerance, and creativity. Our differences, it seems, do not make a difference. However, the young I soon discovered that some dimensions of difference do carry social significance. As a child who did not play with "boys' toys" and identified as gay later, I was often subjected to disdain and hostility from peers and adults.

Ironically, the marginalization comes not only from society at large, but also from within the gay community. A feminine gay man is considered as lesser than his masculine counterpart, because femininity is regarded as weak, unattractive, and second-class. This experience of amplified minority stress prompted me to think about intergroup and intragroup interaction early in life. It has led me to believe that masculinity should not be an indicator of individual worth. Nor should sexuality, skin color, and other identity markers—whether visible or invisible.

His world was the first world, and he was the first god. We could not communicate with him after he had left, but we could see him as if through a piece of glass. We watched as he grew a physical form, coalescing into a man with long silver hair, and we understood why he was called The Oldest. We watched as he molded the world with his hands, stretching and moving spacetime until his world was old like him.

Inductive reasoning is a method of reasoning in which a general principle is derived from a body of observations. It consists of making broad generalizations based on specific observations. If the premises are correct, the conclusion of a deductive argument is certain; in contrast, the truth of the conclusion of an inductive argument is probable, based upon the evidence given.

At the interface between the band insulators LaAlO3 and SrTiO3 sits a two-dimensional electron system with strikingly varied behavior: gate-tunable superconductivity, hints of magnetism, strong spin–orbit coupling and unusual magnetotransport. Whether these effects have a common microscopic origin has been an open question. We report systematic magnetotransport measurements, taken as a function of gate-controlled carrier density, on several interfaces that differ in LaAlO3 thickness and electron mobility. Every sample shows a critical density near 1.7 × 1013 cm−2 where transport switches abruptly from single-carrier to multi-carrier behavior. This density is universal and does not depend on layer thickness or mobility.

The nature of the transition, along with its agreement with spectroscopic data, marks it as a Lifshitz transition, at which electrons start filling the heavier dxz/dyz bands in addition to the light dxy band. We also show that strong spin–orbit interaction and anomalous magnetoresistance set in at this same density. Together, these findings suggest that filling of orbital bands is a unifying principle behind the emergent physics of this oxide interface.

Let ${\cal M}_{g,[n]}$, for $2g-2+n>0$, be the D-M moduli stack of smooth curves of genus $g$ labeled by $n$ unordered distinct points. The main result of the paper is that a finite, connected \'etale cover ${\cal M}^\l$ of ${\cal M}_{g,[n]}$, defined over a sub-$p$-adic field $k$, is "almost" anabelian in the sense conjectured by Grothendieck for curves and their moduli spaces. The precise result is the following.

Let $\pi1({\cal M}^\l{\ol{k}})$ be the geometric algebraic fundamental group of ${\cal M}^\l$ and let ${Out}^*(\pi1({\cal M}^\l{\ol{k}}))$ be the group of its exterior automorphisms which preserve the conjugacy classes of elements corresponding to simple loops around the Deligne-Mumford boundary of ${\cal M}^\l$ (this is the "$\ast$-condition" motivating the "almost" above). Let us denote by ${Out}^*{Gk}(\pi1({\cal M}^\l{\ol{k}}))$ the subgroup consisting of elements which commute with the natural action of the absolute Galois group $G_k$ of $k$. Let us assume, moreover, that the generic point of the D-M stack ${\cal M}^\l$ has a trivial automorphisms group.

Unions stay competitive mostly by showing that they raise total compensation, not just wages. They negotiate better pay, benefits, and job security, which can make union workers more productive by reducing turnover. Unions also compete by organizing aggressively, lobbying for favorable labor laws, and building public support. Many partner with employers on training and safety programs that improve efficiency. This paper provides a novel hierarchical self-supervised learning methodology for medical image segmentation, using multi-domain data aggregation. The research seeks to address the issues of limited annotated databases and low annotation costs in clinical imaging. The proposed approach includes a hierarchical learning hierarchy that rapidly learns from simple to complex tasks, increasing the model's generalization capability. It often provides multi-domain data aggregation to reduce the diversity of the training data, thus increasing the accuracy of the model.

Clinical findings on multiple clinical imaging datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and reliability. This study contributes to the development of self-supervised learning methods in the field of clinical image study, with potential applications in cancer treatment and treatment planning.

Comedian Defends "SNL" ISIS Sketch, Says Ridicule Weakens Terrorists A "Saturday Night Live" sketch showing a young woman leaving home to join ISIS set off a fierce debate on Twitter this week. In response, comedian and commentator Dean Obeidallah has argued that mocking terrorist organizations is a legitimate and effective way to weaken their influence. The sketch parodied an emotional car commercial. Actress Dakota Johnson played a daughter whose father drives her to meet armed militants, and as he tearfully says goodbye, the fighters arrive to collect her. Within hours of the broadcast, social media users were sharply divided.

Some praised the segment as pointed satire. Others condemned it as insensitive, citing the group's killings of hostages and the documented cases of Western teenagers who have traveled to Syria to join it. In a commentary published after the controversy, Obeidallah, a former attorney who has often used comedy to challenge extremism, said critics had misjudged the sketch's purpose. He argued that ISIS depends on an image of strength, discipline and menace, carefully built through polished propaganda videos meant to frighten opponents and attract recruits.

Michels, the famous Dutch coach, has died at the age of 83. Known for his tactics and direction, he was considered one of the greatest coaches in the history of the sport. During his time in office, he took the Dutch to the final of the World Cup in 1974, losing to West Germany. His teaching was characterized by the supremacy of possession, in which the team constantly changed places, confusing the opponents and making them lose their own game.

Michels turned the Dutch team into one of the most successful in the world, and in the finals of the World Cup and the European Cup he took the Dutch in 1988 and twice reached the final. In addition, he coached many clubs to national and international titles, among them Ajax, Barcelona and Bavaria. And he was also known for his character and leadership, which earned him the nickname of "the General". He was a demanding coach, who drove his players to the limit, but at the same time he was known for his ability to animate and encourage them.

"The Education of Robert Nifkin" is a satirical coming-of-age novel set in the 1950s. The story revolves around Robert Nifkin, a witty and unconventional teenager from Chicago who is struggling to fit into the rigid structure of his high school. The novel begins with Robert's admission into Riverview High School, a place he describes as a 'penitentiary designed by a dietitian'. Robert's journey through high school is filled with eccentric characters, including his bohemian parents, a tyrannical principal, and a variety of quirky teachers.

Despite the oppressive environment, Robert manages to maintain his individuality and humor, often resorting to elaborate schemes to avoid attending classes. The turning point in the novel comes when Robert discovers an alternative school, Wheaton, where creativity and independent thinking are encouraged. He manages to transfer to Wheaton, where he thrives and begins to understand the true value of education. Throughout the novel, Robert's witty observations and satirical commentary provide a humorous critique of the American education system. The novel ends with Robert graduating from Wheaton, having learned valuable lessons about individuality, creativity, and the importance of questioning authority.

Logical relations (LR) have been around for many years, and today they are used in many formal results. However, it can be difficult to LR beginners to find a good place to start to learn. Papers often use highly specialized LRs that use the latest advances of the technique which makes it impossible to make a proper presentation within the page limit. This note is a good starting point for beginners that want to learn about LRs. Almost no prerequisite knowledge is assumed, and the note starts from the very basics.

The note covers the following: LRs for proving normalization and type safety of simply typed lambda calculus, relational substitutions for reasoning about universal and existential types, step-indexing for reasoning about recursive types, and worlds for reasoning about references.

The primary goal of brushing is to reduce plaque, as it is the biofilm on your teeth which contribute to tooth decay when exposed to food. It only takes a few minutes for the biofilm to create acidic conditions when you start eating, at which point the'damage is done.' So if your interests are purely dental health, before you eat in the morning and the evening. Brushing immediately after eating can be the worst option, as your teeth are now weakened by exposure to acids, and the brushing process is abrasive.

The combination then can be more damaging than either alone. Waiting an hour should allow your mouth PH to return to normal. So if your interests are'removing bits of food' or what not, an hour after eating. That being said, this can generally be obtained with a simple rinse immediately after eating. TLDR: Before you eat.

The Internet could have two new domain names early next year. The.post and.travel domain names have been approved in principle by the Internet management. They are two of the 10 proposed names that are being evaluated by the Internet administration. These include.porn,.asia,.phone,.antispam,.cat and.post. The.post name has the support of the Universal Postal Union, which wants to use it to identify all postal services and thus facilitate the integration of e-commerce of the national post offices.

The.travel domain name is intended for hotels, travel agencies, air lines, tourist offices, etc., and would allow these to be distinguished from others on the Internet. Support for the name comes from a New York association called The Travel Partnership. The ICANN management said that it was approving the two names in principle after having received from the organizations behind them detailed technical and commercial information. However, the ICANN did not want to imply that the two domains would be available for use. At the same time, the ICANN is evaluating eight other domain names.

Heart-Shaped Box is a horror fiction novel by author Joe Hill, published in 2007 by William Morrow. Aging rock star Judas Coyne is depressed and recovering from a heart attack. His girlfriend has left him and he is haunted by the recent death of his estranged father. Coyne is surprised when a mysterious package arrives in the mail, delivered by UPS. The box contains a ventriloquist's dummy named "Obie" in a heart-shaped box and a CD of an unknown artist, titled "Disco Infernale". The package arrives with no return address.

Coyne is initially unnerved but decides to take the dummy out of the box and assemble it. Upon doing so, he feels a powerful emotional connection to the dummy, which he comes to think of as his "dead twin", the son he never had. Coyne wonders if the dummy is trying to tell him something. Coyne's friend Stacie Phillips, a local TV news reporter, arrives. Coyne shows her the dummy and the CD. Stacie is intrigued by the CD and plays it on Coyne's stereo. The music is dark and eerie. That night, Coyne has trouble sleeping.

Convolutional neural networks owe much of their success on images to the regular grid structure and translation symmetry of the plane, neither of which exists on curved surfaces. Developing deep learning techniques for geometric data is an active and fruitful research area. A common workaround maps a surface to a planar domain and applies a standard CNN, but existing surface-to-image representations either introduce large area distortion or require several images to cover the whole shape. We propose a new representation for sphere-type surfaces based on general covering maps.

Rather than relying on a toric cover with a fixed set of cone points, our construction lets a flat torus wrap around the surface several times, so that every region appears with low distortion somewhere in a single image. Because this image is seamless and periodic, convolution with circular padding is well defined, and off-the-shelf architectures apply with minimal modification. This paper tackles the problem of sphere-type surface learning by developing a novel surface-to-image representation.

Using generic (non)extensive statistics, in which the underlying system autonomously manifests its extensive and nonextensive statistical nature, we extract various fit parameters from the CMS experiment and compare these to the corresponding results obtained from Tsallis and Boltzmann statistics. The present study is designed to indicate the possible variations between the three types of statistical approaches and characterizes their dependence on collision energy, multiplicity, and size of the system of interest.

We analyze the transverse momentum spectra $p_T$ of the strange hadrons \Kslxi produced in Pb+Pb collisions, at 2.76 TeV, in p+Pb collisions, at 5.02 TeV, and in $p+p$ collisions, at 7 TeV. From the comparison of the resulting fit parameters; temperature $T$, volume $V$, and nonextensvie parameter $d$, with calculations based on Tsallis and Boltzmann statistics, remarkable differences between the three types of statistics are determined besides a strong dependence on size and type of the colliding system.

The judge also noted that the sentence should serve as a deterrent to others in positions of power who may be tempted to abuse their positions for personal gain.

The local councils in England are preparing to set the tax increases for next year and will be setting the tax rates and budgets for the next financial year at their upcoming meetings. Councils face higher demands for their services, as they've had to keep them going through the flu pandemic. And they face higher costs, which they say are driven by inflation and the rising cost of energy. The government has warned councils not to raise taxes by too much, or they could face abolition by a new administration after the May elections.

Since the pandemic started, councils have had to find new ways of delivering services, including support for people who hadn't previously needed them. It's expected that the average council tax will rise from £1966 a year to £2045, an increase of £79. The councils had to take over social care, as well as cleaning up the rubbish piled up during the lockdown. David Renard, the leader of Swindon Council, said: "Like many other councils, we've had to take some very difficult decisions about where to make savings.

Federal investigators trying to determine why a Delta Air Lines jet landed on a taxiway instead of the runway in Atlanta on Monday morning say the runway was illuminated, but that approach lights and a ground-based instrument that helps pilots line up with the runway were off. The pilots of the plane that landed at the Atlanta airport have been relieved from flying duties pending probes. The incident happened at Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport, the world's busiest. But it occurred shortly before dawn, when airport operations are slow.

Delta Flight 60, from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, was cleared to land on a main runway around 6:05 a.m., but it landed instead on nearby Taxiway M, which runs parallel to the runway, said FAA spokeswoman Kathleen Bergen. The departure taxiway, which can be filled with aircraft during peak hours, was empty at the time, and the plane landed safely, officials said. No one was injured, and there was no damage to the taxiway. The Boeing 767 aircraft had 182 passengers and a crew of 11. The FAA, the National Transportation Safety Board and Delta Air Lines are investigating.

It happened on a Tuesday, in the cereal aisle of a Kroger in Dayton, Ohio. I was holding a box of bran flakes, reading the fiber content, when it came back to me all at once. Not a voice. Not a vision. Just the plain recollection, the way you suddenly remember where you left your keys. Oh, right. I made all of this. The bran flakes. The fluorescent lights humming overhead. The teenage stock boy with a cold sore, restocking the oatmeal.

The oats themselves, the fields they grew in, the bees that worked those fields, the sun the bees flew under, the hundred billion other suns, and the dark that held them. I remembered deciding on the dark. It had seemed important at the time, to give things somewhere to be lonely. I remembered all of it. Every sparrow, as the saying goes, though the saying undersells it. I remembered the sparrows' lice. I remembered the bacteria in the lice. And I remembered everything that was happening, right now, everywhere. That was the problem.

A complex unit gain graph ($ \mathbb{T} $-gain graph), $ \Phi=(G, \varphi) $ is a graph where the function $ \varphi $ assigns a unit complex number to each orientation of an edge of $ G $, and its inverse is assigned to the opposite orientation. %A complex unit gain graph($ \mathbb{T} $-gain graph) is a simple graph where each orientation of an edge is given a complex unit, and its inverse is assigned to the opposite orientation of the edge. In this article, we propose gain distance matrices for $ \mathbb{T} $-gain graphs.

These notions generalize the corresponding known concepts of distance matrices and signed distance matrices. Shahul K. Hameed et al. introduced signed distance matrices and developed their properties. Motivated by their work, we establish several spectral properties, including some equivalences between balanced $ \mathbb{T} $-gain graphs and gain distance matrices. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of positively weighted $ \mathbb{T} $-gain graphs and study some of their properties. Using these properties, Acharya's and Stani\'c's spectral criteria for balance are deduced. Moreover, the notions of order independence and distance compatibility are studied. Besides, we obtain some characterizations for distance compatibility.

In the philosophy of mind, mind–body dualism denotes either the view that mental phenomena are non-physical, or that the mind and body are distinct and separable. Thus, it encompasses a set of views about the relationship between mind and matter, as well as between subject and object, and is contrasted with other positions, such as physicalism and enactivism, in the mind–body problem.

Aristotle shared Plato's view of multiple souls and further elaborated a hierarchical arrangement, corresponding to the distinctive functions of plants, animals, and humans: a nutritive soul of growth and metabolism that all three share; a perceptive soul of pain, pleasure, and desire that only humans and other animals share; and the faculty of reason that is unique to humans only. In this view, a soul is the hylomorphic form of a viable organism, wherein each level of the hierarchy formally supervenes upon the substance of the preceding level.

Plants lack a nervous system, a brain, and any means of moving from place to place, but they continually sense what is around them and change their behavior accordingly. Over the last few decades, researchers have discovered that plants pass information both within their own bodies and to other organisms through several channels. The word "communication" is used loosely here: it refers to sending and receiving signals that alter behavior, not to conscious intent. Communication Within a Single Plant Electrical signals.

When a leaf is injured, changes in membrane potential can spread to distant parts of the plant within seconds to minutes. In a widely cited 2018 study, Toyota and colleagues used a fluorescent calcium sensor in Arabidopsis to reveal waves of calcium traveling from a caterpillar-damaged leaf to other leaves and setting off defense responses. The Venus flytrap is the most dramatic case: two touches to its trigger hairs within roughly 20 seconds produce action potentials that make the trap snap shut. Hormonal signals. Plant hormones including jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, ethylene, and auxin coordinate growth and defense between tissues.

In Japan, a major banking war is over. The government is returning to its depositors a large share of their savings from savings banks and other financial institutions. It is generally regarded as a victory for the common man who has struggled against huge bank charges for the last few years. In recent years there has been growing criticism of the high costs of bank accounts, especially for low-income households. Some banks charge a yearly percentage of up to 10 percent on top of the interest rate, making it difficult for people to save.

The government has now announced that depositors in savings banks and smaller financial institutions can get most of their savings back, free of charge, following the pressure of consumer groups. According to Reuters, this move will boost consumer confidence, help consumers spend more and increase competition between banks. It is also seen as a break with the controversial cost-cutting methods used by many Japanese banks in recent years, such as reducing the number of branches and introducing automatic customer service. Japanese financial watchdogs have welcomed the news and believe it will make the financial industry more transparent and accountable.

Endogenous or exogenous, dry or wet, various scenarios have been so far depicted for the origin of water on our Solar Systems rocky bodies. Hydrated silicates found in meteorites and in interplanetary dust particles together with observations of abundant water reservoirs in the habitable zone of protoplanetary disks are evidences that support aqueous alteration of silicate dust grains by water vapor condensation in a nebular setting.

We investigate the thermodynamics (temperature and pressure dependencies) and kinetics (adsorption rates and energies, surface diffusion and cluster formation) of water adsorption on surfaces of forsterite grains. (abbreviated) The protoplanetary disk model (ProDiMo) code is tuned to simulate the thermochemical disk structure of the early solar nebula at three evolutionary stages. Pressure, temperature and water vapor abundance within 1 au from the protosun were extracted and used as input for a Monte Carlo code to model water associative adsorption using adsorption energies that resemble the forsterite [100] crystal lattice.

Whether Mercy is the right choice in a given match depends far more on team composition, game mode, and your own skill set than on the nationality of your teammates. Players from China, or from any other region, do not require a particular support hero. That said, there are some practical considerations worth examining when you are coordinating with teammates who may not share your first language. Strengths of Mercy in such situations Mercy is among the heroes least dependent on verbal coordination.

Her core gameplay loop of sustaining a damaged ally, amplifying damage with her blue beam, and resurrecting fallen teammates is largely reactive. You respond to what you observe on screen rather than to callouts. The in-game ping system and communication wheel convey most of the information she needs, such as "I need healing" or "Enemy spotted," and these messages are automatically localized. This makes Mercy a reasonable option when language barriers limit voice communication. Her Guardian Angel mobility also allows her to follow aggressive players closely.
